title: 911 for the Wrong Shade of Blue
summary: Karen reports existential zoning. Operator asks if anyone is bleeding. “Democracy is bleeding, Steven.” Transfer loop until pizza arrives.
visualArc: Kitchen clipboard + purple blinds | 911 fluorescents | pizza doorbell.

title: Big City
summary: Lace Waterfall, Rubella and Lillith's band, travel to a gig in Glamora with gigantic 1980s metal hair already done: airport security, plane, bus terminal, bus roof hatch, taxi sunroof, freight elevator. Nothing fits. They're late; the house guitarist (Kenji, not in the band) covers the solo until the hair comes through the curtain and they walk on to play the rest of Big City. On the final chorus their hair rises through the club skylight and joins the hair-tower skyline. Kenji speaks the tag twice from the wings. Product off-screen. Not the Ultra Screech ad. Alternate arc kept: The Appointment Day.
visualArc: Kenji tag on the empty stage → airport security (a cymbal comes out of the hair) → jet bridge and overhead bins → landing over the hair skyline → bus terminal revolving door → riding the bus through the roof hatch → taxi past the laundromat portholes → the freight elevator yields → Kenji covers the solo as Lace Waterfall walk on → bridge on stage → final chorus → hair through the skylight joins the skyline (drop) → Kenji tag again from the wings.

title: Cat POV
summary: No dialog. The Episode 3 black cat walks Halloween, watches the laser lawn, clocks the Pizza Guy from ankle height, and is still on the driveway when the purple light becomes décor.
visualArc: Sidewalk fur-height → shed serpents → hay bale → pizza shoes → crane from cat → dawn residue → HOA sill.

title: Choose Your Basalt
summary: Dead-pan educational cabaret duet: Lillith and Rubella classify lava types in their gothic living room, then the floor opens onto magma. Ends with “That’s nature for us” / “Science.” before a Twilight Time trance smash-cut.
visualArc: House interior (black lace + Hawaiian leis) → heat shimmer in floorboards → cracked living-room floor → lava tubes beneath the foundation → white-flash smash-cut into trance remix.

title: Chroma Bath
summary: Pure non-representational color. No object at all — no blob, no sphere, no horizon, no figure. Eight segments, each a different processing dialect applied to a swirling color field: ink bleed, video feedback, slit-scan, datamosh, refraction, print misregistration, granulation, bleach. There is no black in the piece; the darkest value is a glowing indigo.
visualArc: Ink bleeding in water → feedback tunnel → slit-scan lanes → compression smear → refraction through turning glass → misregistered print → granular shatter and reassembly → everything bleaches to warm white.

title: Color Whip
summary: Pure non-representational color at warehouse tempo. No object — no blob, no sphere, no horizon, no figure. Eight six-second dialects: strobe invert, whip smear, phosphor stack, smash zoom, channel chase, hard cuts, vortex spin-up, white hit. The slow sibling is Chroma Bath. This one hits.
visualArc: Kick-locked invert → smear streaks → afterimage pile → smash zoom tunnel → RGB plates at three speeds → six hard hue swaps → vortex past readable → one white punch and wreckage.

title: Empty Highway Confession
summary: 4:17 a.m. The driver talks to the radio. Billboard: KEEP GOING. No advertiser.
visualArc: Dashboard glow → needle between stations → lone lit window in a field → KEEP GOING.

title: EyeWash Station Idents
summary: Six analog bumpers: Please Stand By, Rinse Cycle, Unscheduled Programming, Aspect Ratio Matters, We Always Return, 3:44 Again. One still, one sting, one Continuity Voice line each. Nobody comments on the frame.
visualArc: Difficulties card → rinse timer reset → future monitor → fixture nozzles → Biscuit steals the logo → sign-off at 3:44.

title: Cities in the Shell
summary: 2 a.m. oyster bar; each opened shell holds a tiny lit city; she squeezes lemon over one and sets it aside. Tonight's selection is a little metropolitan. Vivienne.
visualArc: Black marble → nacre cities → lemon bead over a boulevard → dark-ocean shell kept.

title: Closed for Cosmic Reasons
summary: Night infinity pool; laminated sign; the water hovers three feet up, still reflecting the city. She sits dry underneath and uses it as a ceiling. Vivienne energy.
visualArc: Chrome stanchion → hovering water sheet → dry woman in the empty basin → smoke flattening on the underside.

title: Complaint Window, Deep Field
summary: A wood-and-brass service window floating in a Hubble field; she slides a triplicate form; stamp: DENIED; now serving: —. Liliane files.
visualArc: Deep-field galaxies → lone booth → triplicate through the slot → DENIED / 000000.

title: Furnace Season
summary: Foundry gala; molten iron as the room's weather; she warms her hands at the pour; sparks die on mink. Vivienne hired a climate.
visualArc: Molten ribbon → bored couture middle distance → hands at the trough → sparks on mink.

title: The Ice That Exhales
summary: Banquet ice sculpture of a woman melting into cigarette smoke, not water; cloth dry; waiter adjusts her a quarter inch. The Two as ice and absence.
visualArc: White linen → ice woman mid-curtsy → smoke not melt → waiter micro-adjustment → empty chair.

title: The Moon Is Collect
summary: Red rotary, taut cord to a huge moon, empty chair, abandoned gloves. Someone is calling collect; the charges are astronomical; she stepped out. Liliane energy.
visualArc: Red plastic on black lacquer → cord out the window → moon as the other party → empty gloves.

title: The Overnight Conservator
summary: 3 a.m. gallery; she dusts a kouros; it holds her champagne; she holds its broken forearm like a clipboard. Post-gala Two. Sibling hour to Master Control.
visualArc: Hard museum spot → torn ballgown → kouros with flute → condition report in lipstick.

title: Third Shift Porcelain
summary: Couture mannequins at a factory time-clock; one smokes chrome in the dock door. Beauty is hourly; overtime is not discussed. The Two do not punch out.
visualArc: Marble lineup → time-clock → chrome cigarette in the dock → red LED in 4/4.

title: Gallery Fog / Caffeinated Melon
summary: Espresso-hooked melon emits honesty fog. Ninety seconds of truth. Then everyone pretends. Justine eats crackers.
visualArc: White cube → melon + tubes → fog → frozen confessions → clap.

title: Home Sweet Void
summary: After the cockpit cruise they are inside. Greeting is the jumbo Earth marshmallow bag on the glass table. Conversation (space speeding) starts before the floor. White asteroid-ride worms sneak the baseboard, sit up as a cut, and hog the scene. The white building cat speaks once and is stopped by glow, not a beam. Daisy, Hanshaw, and the bird joke remain this week's musical spine — this packet waits its turn for Imagine generation.
visualArc: Pad into table / bag down → marshmallow talk → floor sneak → one head turns → hard cut to seated hog → Earth coffee-house cup → cat glow-stop → bag was here first.

title: We Play to Win (House of Mirrors Rally)
summary: Vivienne and Liliane play ping-pong in a ruined ballroom. Plaster falls. They do not flinch. Pizza box on the intact half of the table.
visualArc: Chandelier ballroom → rally → plaster dust → chin tilt → split table + pizza.

title: Item Three: Decorative Accent
summary: Emergency HOA meeting. The purple driveway light is tabled as a decorative accent. Brad has swatches. Biscuit steals the gavel. Pizza Guy at the door.
visualArc: Fluorescent clubhouse → cracked gavel → violet blinds → rift through the window → pizza in the doorway.

title: 2AM Laundromat Slow Dance
summary: Two unnamed strangers fold a sheet, then slow-dance between dryers. The attendant mops around them. EyeWash always on in the corner.
visualArc: Fluorescent rows → shared sheet → dance in dryer glow → attendant mop → sign-off TV.

title: Marble Tick Tack: Wrong Sets
summary: Sibling of the night-lot take on the same instrumental. Magnets never notice while a generating intelligence swaps the episode: horseshoe cabinet, Halbach desert, hopping mountain lion in the woods, Meissner ice, Helmholtz saucer, London maglev under a flower tandem, Seoul non-contact gears, ferrofluid smash, souvenir fridge magnets chaining home. Station objects hop; magnets travel. Roley Voss grammar, jokier sets.
visualArc: Cabinet horseshoe + prompt bar → desert inpaint → Halbach skate / eddy slow-fall → woods inpaint + hopping lion → Chladni / cow magnet / magnetostriction → ice Meissner Almost → space Helmholtz bottle + vinyl-toy aliens → London maglev / flower tandem → Seoul gears → quiet viewing-film aurora / hung ferrofluid → thaw smash → souvenir parade → Gauss marble while sets peel → cabinet chain lock → 3s decay, cursor dead.

title: Marble Tick Tack
summary: Pure animation bridge at 136 BPM. No faces. Cabinet marble chorus walks one night lot: doorway onto a dirt alley where spheres jump a visible gap to slam together and then gear without touching around a copper Rodin torus, then an unreal green lawn whose three coils fire a rotating field while a dumbbell rod pair tumbles end-over-end and the magnet tower stands on the 68 BPM kick and slumps in the gap, then frozen ferrofluid rain at the dirt/grass seam — a bound pair in mutual orbit rolls home and jumps the last gap into a Gauss chain on the same shelf. Cylinders spin on their ends and precess; the rooms vibrate on the eighths. Dancers hop, magnets orbit. Roley Voss lane.
visualArc: Warm cabinet / 136 BPM hop and a counter-rotating disc stack → cube slide to glasses → doorway jump gap → dirt alley → Rodin cyclotron with a disc spinning on the top winding → jump gap into non-contact magnetic gears → fence-gap Almost → electromagnet tower rise/slump → three-phase orbit plus end-over-end rod tumble → hung ferrofluid and standing rods vibrating → quiet Almost → thaw smash → bound pair in mutual orbit home past the dry Rodin → jump gap into the cabinet chain lock → 3s decay on a disc spinning down.

title: Master Control, 4 AM
summary: Oz logs a timecode. One monitor shows this room a few seconds ahead. He stands up to top off his tea. He does not look at the monitor. “It's not haunted, it's unscheduled.”
visualArc: CRT wall → thermos → future-monitor offset → empty chair, still airing.

title: Molten Silver Sphere
summary: Pure visual cutaway: a glossy molten silver liquid-metal sphere hovers in a pitch-black cave, pulsating to an unseen deep beat while cavern walls snap between high-contrast checkerboard and electric neon line grids. Three maxed-detail video prompt variations — slow zoom, orbital neon veins, and macro chromium dive.
visualArc: Black cavern void → hovering chrome sphere → checkerboard ↔ neon wall flashes → chromatic reflections on liquid metal → camera closes in (zoom / orbit / macro).

title: Monster Mash Finale
summary: Rubella covers "The Monster Mash" on the post-snake-battle lawn while a cursed monster party erupts — Nixon, Furbies, knife-kittens, Skeksis and more. Amy and Alec return from the hiking sketch in full costume to dance, a Thriller-style werewolf moonwalks the perimeter, Lillith runs a parallel spy heist, and the hologram reveal tips into a Spy vs. Spy noir outro.
visualArc: Lawn aftermath → sing-us-out cold open → Rubella at silver mic → cursed party montage → Amy & Alec dance in hiking costume → Lillith bedroom heist → party escalation → Thriller werewolf moonwalk → hologram glitch → white/black spy stalk → gadget standoff → cut to black.

title: Morning After the Portal
summary: Golden-hour cul-de-sac cleanup. Someone power-washes a sigil. Pizza Guy now delivering breakfast burritos.
visualArc: Dawn cul-de-sac → bathrobe neighbors → purple residue in GLASS ONLY → burrito pizza guy.

title: Mountain Lion Wildflower Field
summary: POV leash: a mountain lion insists on showing us a field. Flowers escalate into botanical surrealism, then give way to open ocean and come back bigger and stranger on the far shore. Arrival: a sunlit clearing already full of other mountain lions. Two Minimax beds at 110 BPM — the ocean crossing IS the crossfade from Come Further into Here They Are. No swimming, no peril. Do not run 2 minutes of drag.
visualArc: Insistent look-back in a real meadow → oversized lupine tunnel → painted + photoreal flower architecture → the field becomes the sea → crossing open water on a causeway of floating blooms → far shore where the flowers return larger and more painted → sun-stunned multi-lion clearing → gratifying hold.

title: Article Seven
summary: Mandatory funk interval. Plastic steward reads the laminated card. Remaining time is always fourteen minutes. The lawn is on break.
visualArc: Frozen lasers → ON BREAK sign → stretches, no dancing → Pizza Guy crossing guard → clock still 3:44.

title: Call Forty-Seven
summary: Karen reports existential zoning. Each transfer adds a bar of hold music. Democracy is bleeding, Steven. The call never drops.
visualArc: Kitchen cordless → swatches vs driveway → dispatch CALL #47 → sticker → own voicemail → pizza doorbell, still holding.

title: Closed Since Ninety-Eight
summary: Two reflections leave a house of mirrors in the wrong car. The radio is a station that signed off in 1998. Harmony is always one bar late.
visualArc: Tuner parked on 1998 → wrong lot arm-in-arm → rearview singing last bar → ten and two → dead studio furniture → taillights, passenger late.

title: Empty Parking Lot Waltz
summary: Last two people in a vast wet lot. They could go or they could stay. The last chord never arrives.
visualArc: Two cars → rumpled dress on a door → orbit without touching → unresolved.

title: Haunted or Unscheduled
summary: Master Control 4 AM underscore — Rhodes four-note loop that never develops, 3:44 twice identically, program bleed on the second pass. Not a second sign-off.
visualArc: Rack hum → Rhodes loop → optional Continuity Voice → 3:44 → 3:44 again with bleed → unresolved.

title: Heart Rate Optimal
summary: A heart-rate alert that thinks it is a ballad. 78 and 78. The chorus would like to go to ninety; the watch does not approve.
visualArc: Watch face 78/78 → still woman closes a ring → ELEVATED chime at the same tempo → cracker, latte, robot → OPTIMAL.

title: Heels or No Entry
summary: A rooftop bouncer recites the door policy while the skyline burns. She produces emergency stilettos. The kick arrives after Approved.
visualArc: Velvet rope + burning skyline → closed list → stilettos from the purse → she changes shoes → inside like Tuesday → Approved on the click.

title: Neon Exit Sign
summary: Series signature. Wet alley of EXIT signs that never lead outside. The Two only as reflections. Don't smudge the mascara.
visualArc: Flickering EXIT tube → heels on wet centerline → compact-mirror flames → closed-loop alley.

title: Pepperoni or Margherita
summary: Fifteen seconds of cheerful ad, hard cut, then a deadpan ballad about arriving when chaos peaks.
visualArc: Box at chest height → laser battle soft → walking away without looking back.

title: Porch Light Meridian
summary: Crane up from a porch bulb after chaos. The yard is small but the sky will not fit.
visualArc: Pizza box / porch circle → roofs → moon with a wrong second glow.

title: Quarter to Seventy-Five
summary: No chorus — only the title phrase, a clock stuck at 3:44, and an FM needle drifting left.
visualArc: Mercury streetlamps → frozen 3:44 → café looped three times → empty road.

title: Receipt Dated Thursday
summary: Continuity Voice reads a poodle’s return receipt from a store that will not exist until Thursday. The barcode is always one digit short.
visualArc: Thermal slip → heist under chairs → incomplete scan → rift lot → receipt in the minutes → return, still short.

title: Rinse Cycle
songTitle: Rinse Cycle (Fifteen Minutes, Do Not Blink)
summary: Sign-off theme. Comfort that curdles on the second pass. Nine-bar phrases, late resolutions.
visualArc: Eyewash fixture ident → empty master control → test pattern that blinks like an eye → 3:44 again.

title: Static Between Stations
summary: The dial left between two songs on purpose. Dashboard glow, mercury streetlamps, laundromat fluorescents humming with the hiss.
visualArc: Tuner needle in the gray → mercury blur → fluorescent hum.

title: Strange Light
summary: Sun and moon sharing one daylight sky. One witness. Quiet cosmic lawbreaking. Complements the Episode 3 crane.
visualArc: Quiet street → dual celestial bodies → two-direction shadows → color carried home.

title: The Laundromat Saints
summary: Two strangers alternate lines like strangers who accidentally agree. Dryer thumps on bar 5. Diegetic EyeWash TV, then full score for the slow dance.
visualArc: Four washers apart → slow orbit → dance between dryers → buzzer cuts mid-phrase.

title: The Most Refreshing Drink
summary: EyeWash sponsor for an over-engineered glass of ice water. Apparatus clicks in the dark lab; the gulp lands a beat before the ice. No sung lead.
visualArc: Dark lab LEDs → window apparatus in noon sun → laminar droplets → early gulp / late ice → repeat uncorrected → hovering cube, small print.

title: The Roof Knows How to Wait
songTitle: The Roof Knows How to Wait
summary: Rubella inventories a ceiling that has not fallen yet. Natural ventilation. The extra bar is the plaster still deciding.
visualArc: Hole and stars → low chandelier → bored under the draft → glasses and berries → chandelier keeps its job → extra bar, piano late.

title: This Program Contains Dialogue
episode: EyeWash Station / The Long Way Up
summary: Pre-program warning sung as a hymn. S&P will not stamp until someone talks. The card never changes.
visualArc: DIALOGUE card → lectern → legal crawl → unstamped PROBABLY FINE → off-mic “Is this on.”

title: Ultra Screech (Glam-Sham-Poo)
summary: Joke TV commercial for Ultra Screech Formula, conformed to the 2:51 Ultra Screech 2 bed with the take-1 scream spliced on. Cold-open scream, Kenji hype, laundry-room dual frontwomen, salaryman panic, product bottle, HOA/handbook trade, club glam, bridge solo, vending-machine logo. Original 5-still package is the spine; office stills only on shouting samples.
visualArc: Cold-open scream → Kenji hero pitch → laundry-room Rubella + Lillith → office samples → product bottle chorus → neon-pour / HOA citation trade → handbook §12 → club glam chant → bridge argument + solo → logo / vending-machine outro.

title: Neon Nightfall
summary: A neon‑lit alley chase with a hovering drone, rain‑slick walls, and a flashing billboard. The video drives a synth‑wave Minimax bed with drops for drone swoop and billboard flash.
visualArc: Drone darts past runner → rain‑slick chase → billboard flash freezes action → siren rise → chase resumes into high‑energy chorus.

title: No Other Human Sounds
episode: Episode 05 candidate (insert — cut-through, then the cliff)
summary: Rubella and Riley walk the unmaintained cut-through and fall into a short-line rally. They rejoin Lillith and drive to Pulpit Overlook. Rosencrantz dialog alts: silence wager, Smith as coin flip, waiting for the repeater. The last name is Smith. The tower stays offscreen. The car does not go up.
visualArc: 5:40 PM fork → needle road → rally two-shot → eight-second stop → idle at the canopy break → picnic table on a cliff, the drop, no tower.

title: Ping-Pong vs. AI Robot Showdown
summary: Pong-Bot 3000 vs the ladies. Biscuit steals the ball. The robot does not want to be turned off. Justine: “If we lose, I'm buying the robot a latte.”
visualArc: Neon café → glowing ball trail → Biscuit on the table → USB heart toss.

title: Please Stand By
summary: Full-frame TECHNICAL DIFFICULTIES card. Everything happens in the audio. Never cut away.
visualArc: One card. The image never changes. That is the shot.

title: Riley Was a Space Cop
summary: HSV table is the door: Alright, you caught me. I used to be a space cop, okay? Cut to nineteen at Transportation Patrol Annex. Years of two lines and one cube, nights, a yard over a canyon, Appendix C, then a bestowal — hollow-chevron wings, an odd short sword, a hymn that also files. She inhales for the first posting. Rubella cuts: we are expected back down to Earth, right away. Not a fight movie. Scenery beds hold the black hole; rooms stay short.
visualArc: Table door → orbit scenery → first-year cube → nights / window planet → empty canyon yard → further exercises → Appendix C hold → bestowal + theme → two-moon sky (unfinished posting) → sage-crop return.

title: Rubella Stand-Up
summary: Item Seven: Resident Comments. The podium is a laundry-room intercom. Madelyn put her on the list. Folding chairs creak; they do not clap. Spoken Voice bed, not a musical.
visualArc: Podium lock → detergent relic → heckle wide (she does not turn) → land with duplicate forms.

title: The Seed Casts Twice
summary: Noir paper street. The theft is already over; the second cast is still happening. A child's shadow stays planted on the third step and blooms into a fractal garden. Breath iterates the plants; a hold withdraws them; a flat seed-disc drops into the palm. Lotte Reiniger table, Desmet amber field. Not Daisy. Ladies off the street.
visualArc: Empty street + orphan shadow → child matched then split → canopy hides the disc → hold withdraws branches → disc on the palm, shadow locks.

title: Short Packet Farm — Generate-First Boards
summary: The three boarded packets off the joke / strange-3D farm: a 5s seamless loop tile, a 7s joke interrupt, and a 30s strange-3D gag. One room each, one job each, no faces, no lipsync. Full boards in prompts/short-packet-farm-segments.md.
visualArc: Mail-room bag orbit at chest height → clubhouse chair that unfolds into a second chair → brass lamp that approves the form, the desk, the stamp and finally itself.

title: Short Packet Farm — Joke Interrupts
summary: Ten 3–10s interrupts on the cowboy-chimp / bird-flock shelf. Building bureaucracy: forms, inventory, HOA, elevators, bags at chest height. Cut in, echo a prior line off camera, land one physical punch, cut out. No faces, one line maximum, never on screen.
visualArc: Napkin that will not end → PROBABLY FINE → a sign that lowers itself → chairs creaking in unison → a cage tagged 1 → an extinguisher on a tag hook → a parking row shoved over → a chute that refolds your form → lint by the counted sheet → forty chairs in rows at the curb.

title: Short Packet Farm — Strange 3D
songTitle: Third Shift Porcelain (kick is a stamp on marble)
summary: Thirteen packets of objects with jobs, doing the job wrong or too well. Porcelain, marble insert, honey-oak, brass, wet enamel on the ground only, geometric white panels, short honeycomb guards. Locked camera or slow orbit. No HUD, no lightning, no nebula — these things are employed.
visualArc: Loop tiles: a form that splits and rejoins, enamel in the grout, a cube on detents, a key cabinet that audits, a fan with one empty cell, a scale that tares itself, a tap that always finds the same hex, a tube carrier that arrives empty. Gag sketches: a dock floor that rises to meet policy, a directory that costs a floor, a lift with a counteroffer, a balance that weighs its own pan, a cabinet that files itself.

title: Skeleton Union Break
summary: Battle freezes. Plastic skeleton holds ON BREAK. Fifteen-minute groove reset per contract. Pizza Guy as crossing guard. Score: Article Seven.
visualArc: Frozen lasers → laminated break sign → stretches → resume on the downbeat.

title: Spooky Telephone Poles
summary: Halloween sidewalk pseudoscience lecture: Lillith, Rubella, and Scarlet explain why utility poles are spooky — rat electrocution, ground current, hydrogen sulfide, sewer-pipe bracing — then lean away in unison. Button line: “And that’s why you have to dodge phone poles!”
visualArc: Wet Halloween sidewalk → crackle at utility pole → dead-pan lecture trio → synchronized dodge past the pole → keep walking.

title: The 480p Studio Huddle
summary: Grainy 480p feed into the Meta-Studio: Rubella, Lillith, and writer Mara argue cereal bowls, barista informants, and Ep2 pacing under one harsh softbox — until Mara seeds the HOA Meeting and a one-octave synth bass conspiracy cue.
visualArc: Warehouse + camera crane → softbox folding-chair huddle → cereal storyboard slap → barista print point → Mara scribbling → 480p static / standby.

title: The Long Way Up
summary: The wordy episode — same juxtaposition family as Monster Mash (1958) on a laser-snake lawn and Rubella's monkey science: wrong channel, full commitment. Three women drive up a hill and walk the rest. Dialog versions: V2 Mulholland open → V3 daytime interview; Rosencrantz register (probability trucks, climbing metaphysics, padlock mood). One boot and one stiletto. Fourteen seconds of silence at the saddle.
visualArc: 2:10 PM county road (contract crawl) → sedan interview → ordinance gate → hood up → switchbacks → blue-hour saddle → fire under a black tower.

title: The Soft Gyre
summary: A house-sized translucent gel blob hovers above anvil thunderheads, spins, and throws sparks and jello at the weather. Clouds dent, lantern, and grow glass flowers. The gyre spins clockwise; every ejecta counter-rotates. Five locked stills, ready to animate.
visualArc: Hover above the deck → jello weather + dented cloud → interior helix and cloud-bubbles → vapor tendril answers → pull-back, halo, glass flower, undersun flare.

title: Ultra-Refreshed Water Lab
summary: The most refreshing glass of ice water in human history, delivered by an insanely complex window apparatus. Played completely straight.
visualArc: Dark neon lab → sunlit apparatus → laminar droplets → slow-motion gulp.

title: The Velvet Rope at the End of the World
summary: Bouncer enforces heels-or-no-entry while the skyline burns. She produces emergency stilettos. Approved.
visualArc: Velvet rope → ash → compact stilettos → mirrorball vs burning city.

title: Well Fall
summary: POV down a real well, instrumental heavy metal, no vocal. Lip is locked. Click a sight into open slots B–G, or an ending into H — previews fill [SIGHT] in the prompts.
visualArc: Stone well mouth → drop (riff in) → open sight B → open sight C → open sight D → open sight E → open sight F → open sight G → bottom or none.

title: Yacht Guitar Orchestra
summary: Rubella and Lillith sunbathing on a yacht while a guitar line plays the rail. Three-song hard-cut journey in twenty silent Imagine scenes (about 3:24, working times): daylight vine island with guitar orchestra bed, dark island fire with Wallisian bed, night approach to Busan Gwangan Bridge with Korean K-pop bed. Every mouth stays closed, the vocals are off-picture. No landing.
visualArc: Open ocean lounges + guitar line → the sway, prow and wake, a chord ripple down the necks → sunglasses reflect the vine island → shore cannons, a pick over the rail, one dolphin leap, too many parrots → hard cut dark: lights in the vines, beach fire, faces and a cannon in firelight, the parrots leave, the lounges in the dark → hard cut night: Busan Gwangan Bridge RGB + Marine City, light on the hull, the ring from above, a strip of black water that never closes.
